display.title: Episode 230: The Hour of Fortune
display.summary_short: A loyal servant gets one hour in the king's treasure room but spends it listening to music. Uncle Yossi explains that this world is the treasure room and mitzvos are the treasures.
display.summary_long: Uncle Yossi opens with the great marches of Jewish history: leaving Mitzrayim through the sea, crossing the Jordan with Yehoshua, and going up to the Beis HaMikdash three times a year, and says the next grand parade will be with Moshiach, so we must practice now. After the Hakochainik march, a Beis Rivkah student says the Shema in Studio 604. The story: the king's most faithful servant, Yisroel, is given one hour in the royal treasure room to take whatever he wants, and brings ten empty barrels. But the king, testing him, places a violinist in the room, and each time Yisroel reaches for the diamonds a lovelier tune begins. The hour ends and he leaves empty-handed. Uncle Yossi explains the parable: the King is Hashem, we are the servant, this world is the treasure room, the mitzvos are the treasures, and the music is the yetzer hara trying to distract us. The show closes with an invitation to get a letter in the new children's Sefer Torah, a sponsor message and more names in the Sefer Torah contest.
display.lesson: Our time in this world is a precious hour to gather mitzvos; do not let the yetzer hara distract you.
